briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Momentum Builds in Lansing While D.C. Circuit Backs Rescheduling and Psilocybin Nears the Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax is under real political pressure as a bipartisan repeal push gains steam, even as new stores and product rollouts show operators still finding growth. Nationally, a federal appeals court just upheld medical marijuana's move to Schedule III and Compass Pathways' psilocybin program keeps clearing regulatory hurdles toward a 2027 launch.

local.text: U.S. Senate candidate John James is now publicly backing repeal of Michigan's 24% wholesale marijuana tax, giving the relief push new political weight as lawmakers from both parties line up behind it.
A Republican state representative has introduced House Bill 6224 to fully repeal the wholesale tax, calling it an unnecessary burden — real legislative traction operators can point to.

The tax is also undercutting its own case for survival: it generated roughly $37 million in Q2 and $34 million in Q1, far below the $105 million-per-quarter projection — ammunition repeal advocates are using in Lansing.

Grön's bestselling "Pearls" gummies just landed on Michigan shelves as part of a four-state rollout, already confirmed at Pure Options, High Profile, and Lume — a sign brands still see Michigan as worth chasing.
A new dispensary, Blue Sky Cannabis Co., soft-opened in downtown Ann Arbor next to Spores Cafe — fresh proof that new retail concepts are still launching in the market despite the tax headwinds.

national.text: The D.C. Circuit just handed rescheduling backers a win: on Sept. 9 the court left the medical marijuana Schedule III order in effect, rejecting arguments that opponents had shown they'd be harmed by the change.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin program keeps clearing hurdles: six-month Phase 3 data confirmed a rapid and durable response, with commercial launch-readiness on track for the end of 2026 and launch expected in first half of 2027.

The FDA has scheduled its first public hearing on the potential future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs for Sept. 14, 2026, following final clinical trial guidance covering psilocybin, LSD and MDMA.

Trump signed H.R. 6500 on Sept. 2, pushing the federal hemp-derived THC restrictions from Nov. 12 to Dec. 11 and giving brands another month of runway while Congress drafts a permanent regulatory framework.

MSO Vireo Growth keeps expanding its buying spree beyond plant-touching assets — an $88.5 million New York real estate purchase and a $40 million ag-supply acquisition in the same week — while also positioning to become Florida's third-largest operator via its Fluent deal.
